newsitem.title: MEXICO: Coca-Cola Mexico unit '96 market share up.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Mexico unit '96 market share up.

text.p: Coca Cola de Mexico, the Mexican unit of Coca Cola Co, will invest $250 million in 1997 and expects sales volume growth of 8 percent against 5 percent last year, the chairman of the company said Monday.

Jose Octavio Reyes Lagunes, chairman of Cola-Cola de Mexico, told a media conference that soft drinks prices in 1997 would rise in tandem with Mexican inflation and added Coca-Cola's Mexican market share increased 4 percentage points in 1996 to 65 percent, with sales of 1.3 billion cases.

"We consistently grow above the rates of the industry...At the end of 1996 the market share of Coca-Cola products in general was a little more than 65 percent, winning four percentage points over the previous year," Reyes said.

On the planned investment, Reyes said the company would look to consolidate and expand on product lines launched in 1996. Of the planned investment, $150 million will go to infrastructure and the rest to marketing strategies, he said. In 1996 the company invested $269 million.
Talking about the sales volume increase, Reyes said flavored drinks would rise 10 percent and the Coca-Cola brand would rise six percent in 1997.
Through a network of 19 distributors in Mexico, it sells the brands Diet Coke, Fanta, Sprite and Lift.
On the outlook for drinks prices, Reyes said movements would match inflation and that over the whole year, increases would work out at similar levels to consumer prices.
